claims.claim: Thomas V. Brocklehurst released a pair of grey squirrels at Henbury Park near Macclesfield in 1876.
claims.episode_span: In 1876 Victorian banker Thomas V. Brocklehurst released a pair of eastern grey squirrels he had brought from New York into Henbury Park near Macclesfield, Cheshire.
claims.supporting_quote: Thomas V. Brocklehurst released a pair of Greys that he brought back from a business trip to America into Henbury Park

claims.claim: 61% of 223 grey squirrels tested positive for parapoxvirus antibodies while only 2.86% of 140 red squirrels showed exposure.
claims.episode_span: A 2000 study in Animal Conservation tested 223 apparently healthy grey squirrels and found 61 percent carried antibodies to the parapoxvirus, while only 2.86 percent of 140 red squirrels showed exposure and three of those displayed active disease.
claims.source_title: Grey squirrels have high seroprevalence to a parapoxvirus associated with deaths in red squirrels
claims.supporting_quote: A high percentage (61%) of apparently healthy grey squirrels, were found to have been exposed to the parapoxvirus. Only 2.86% (4/140) of red squirrels had antibody and three of these animals had parapoxvirus-associated disease.

claims.claim: Grey squirrel damage to trees and woodlands is estimated to cost around £37 million per year.
claims.episode_span: The Forestry Commission later recorded that grey squirrels strip bark from trees, reducing timber quality and imposing an estimated £37 million annual cost.
claims.source_title: Grey squirrels: managing an invasive species to support woodlands and our native red squirrels
claims.supporting_quote: This damage is estimated to cost around £37 million per year, 1 representing a significant threat to the potential economic growth, productivity and resilience of our woods and forests.
